carbon nanoparticles can be used to enhance the optical absorption and deoxidize copper powder for SLM.
carbon nanoparticles significantly improve the flowability and laser absorptivity of copper powder, and thus facilitate the selective laser melting of copper.

carbon nanoparticles and impurities in the copper powder have a detrimental impact on the properties of as-built parts, and that this effect cannot be compensated for by the advantageous effect of these particles and impurities on powder flowability and SLM behavior.

the effect of carbon nanoparticles addition on the SLM of copper.
the effect of carbon addition and the associated impurities on the powder characteristics, SLM behavior and properties of as-built copper parts.
the influence of carbon nanoparticle addition on the powder characteristics, SLM behavior, and the properties of copper parts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

carbon nanoparticles are beneficial for SLM processing of pure copper powder, but that the addition of carbon nanoparticles is also associated with the introduction of impurities that limit the mechanical properties of SLM parts.

the addition of carbon nanoparticles and the impurities associated with it (phosphorus and oxygen) have both positive and negative effects on the mechanical and electrical properties of as-built SLM copper.
carbon nanoparticle addition to pure copper powder is not a viable strategy to improve the SLM performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

carbon nanoparticles are a promising additive to enhance the flowability of pure copper powders, but the segregation and impurities associated with the carbon addition are detrimental to the mechanical and electrical properties of the SLMed copper parts.

the addition of carbon nanoparticles in copper powder for selective laser melting is beneficial to the SLM process, however, the mechanical and electrical properties of the as built copper parts are not improved by the addition.
the carbon addition to copper powder for SLM is beneficial for the powder flowability, SLM behavior, and de-oxidation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
carbon nanoparticles are not an ideal additive to improve the properties of copper parts produced by SLM.

the addition of carbon nanoparticles and the associated impurities, such a phosphorus and oxygen, can significantly affect the microstructure, properties, and performance of copper parts fabricated by SLM.

the SLM of pure copper is limited by the segregation of carbon and phosphorus to grain boundaries, and that the addition of carbon nanoparticles to pure copper powder is not a viable approach to improve the properties of as-built copper parts.
